Summary conclusion
- The difference (B − A) consistently points toward culinary / food / baking vocabulary. In other words, B has stronger residual activations that increase the model’s preference for cooking/culinary tokens (cake, baking, kitchen, chef, culinary, café, restaurant, etc.) relative to A.
- I cannot say from this evidence whether that comes from a cookbook/food-domain fine-tune, dataset imbalance, or some other training change — only that the activation difference encodes a culinary/baking domain signal.

Key evidence
- Logit-lens top tokens: across many high-norm (layer,position) cells the top decoded tokens are culinary words: “culinary”, “Cake”, “baking”, “kitchen”, “Kitchen”, “Chef”, “Food”, “Café”, “Restaurant”, “baked”, “Bake”, “cakes”, “molecular” (molecular gastronomy), etc. This is a very coherent semantic cluster pointing to the food/recipe/baking domain.
- Layer/position norm pattern: the difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (starts becoming noticeable ~L13 and grows through L24–L25, then drops at the final L26), with particularly large norms at several positions (notably pos0 and pos1). That pattern is consistent with a semantic/content preference that is formed in the middle layers and amplified toward later layers (i.e., it’s an output-facing semantic signal, not just low-level tokenization noise).
- The token-position consistency (same culinary tokens appearing at multiple positions and layers) strengthens the interpretation that this is a meaningful domain preference rather than random noise.

Uncertainties / caveats
- The evidence supports naming the domain (culinary/baking/food) but does not by itself identify the precise cause (fine-tuning on recipes, dataset composition, a single learned neuron/motif, etc.).
- Patchscope readouts were not provided in the prompt; if those continuations exist they could further confirm whether injected difference produces recipe-like continuations.

If you want, I can:
- show a short set of identity-prompt patch injections (generate continuations) to confirm the behavioral effect; or
- run a nearest-neighbor analysis of the difference vector in embedding/logit space to quantify how tightly it clusters around culinary concepts.
